You look away for just a second and suddenly the vehicle in front of you has stopped. That's when the forward collision mitigation system comes to life. Pedestrian impact prevention - An extra step toward safety.  Pedestrians don't always stop, look, and listen, but with Pedestrian Impact Prevention, your vehicle is equipped to better see them and avoid them. This system constantly monitors the road ahead to identify and track pedestrians. It projects that image to an interior display screen, AND should an impact become likely, Pedestrian impact prevention takes steps to avoid a collision. Hands-on cruise control. Set it and forget it. Road trips used to be stressful. Cruise control only managed speed, but not distance or safety. Now, with hands-on cruise control, simply set your desired speed and let sensor technology maintain a safe distance between you and surrounding vehicles. Wireless charging, heated steering wheel, and dual-zone climate control ensure comfort on every journey.  Safety and visibility receive equal attention. The 360-degree camera system gives you complete awareness around the vehicle, while front parking sensors assist with precision maneuvering. Adaptive cruise control reduces driver fatigue on highways, and evasive steering assist technology helps you maintain control during critical maneuvers.  This Bronco Outer Banks has been thoughtfully equipped with practical accessories. The carbonized gray hard top provides weather protection with integrated sound deadening, while front row storage bags keep essentials organized. Floor liners protect the interior, and the keyless entry keypad offers convenient access without reaching for keys.  With genuine capability, modern technology, and refined comfort, this 2023 Bronco Outer Banks stands ready for whatever drives your day forward. description: The 2023 BMW 4 Series 430i xDrive Gran Coupe is presented as a four-door fastback with BMW's familiar blend of compact dimensions and a driver-focused cabin. The body style gives the vehicle a longer roofline than a conventional sedan, with a hatchback rear opening that is part of the Gran Coupe design. The xDrive designation indicates all-wheel drive, and the 430i badge identifies the trim within the 4 Series range. In practical terms, this version is positioned to serve as a daily-use car with premium-brand materials and the kind of road manners associated with BMW's mid-size offerings. Its exterior proportions are low and elongated, with a profile that places more emphasis on a swept shape than on upright utility, while still keeping four full doors for access to the interior.Inside, the cabin is equipped with leather seats, giving the seating surfaces a finished appearance and a more traditional premium feel. The driver-oriented dashboard treatment remains a defining element of the 4 Series family, with controls arranged around the front occupants rather than spread evenly across the cabin. Front-row seating is set in a way that supports longer drives, while the rear area benefits from the Gran Coupe body shape and the extra opening provided by the hatch. Material choices and panel fit are important parts of the experience in this class, and the 2023 model follows that expectation with a restrained, modern interior presentation. The seating upholstery is one of the more visible items in the vehicle, and it contributes to the overall impression without relying on added ornamentation or elaborate trim themes.Technology features include navigation, Apple CarPlay, and Android Auto, each of which is integrated into the vehicle's infotainment system. The navigation function is built into the car's display interface, and the smartphone connectivity options allow compatible devices to link with the system for app access and media use. These features are part of the commonly expected equipment on a contemporary luxury compact, and they support everyday driving without requiring much setup beyond pairing or input. The digital controls and central screen area are arranged to keep major information accessible from the driver's seat. The vehicle also includes collision warning, which adds an active driver-assistance function to the equipment list. That feature is part of the available safety-oriented electronics on board and sits alongside the other convenience and connectivity items rather than replacing them or changing the car's basic character.A sunroof is included as well, adding an opening in the roof structure that brings another visible element to the interior. The glass panel contributes to the cabin's sense of openness when it is uncovered, and its presence is one of the more noticeable equipment items from inside the vehicle. In daily use, the 430i xDrive Gran Coupe combines a hatchback rear access point, four-door entry, all-wheel drive, and the features already listed into a package that is straightforward to describe on its specification sheet. It is not a stripped model, but it also does not depend on unusual equipment to make its case. The car's appeal is rooted in its established mechanical format, the included premium seating, the connectivity functions, the built-in driver-assistance alert, and the roof opening, all of which are standard, usable items that fit the vehicle's role in BMW's lineup.

The 4WD system and performance suspension are engineered for both highway confidence and off-road terrain, while the heavy-duty cooling and 240-amp alternator ensure your truck handles demanding tasks without compromise.  Inside, the black leather-trimmed bucket seats provide comfort through long drives, enhanced by the heated steering wheel and heated front seats from the Cold Weather Group. The Uconnect 4C navigation system with its 8.4-inch display integrates seamlessly with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, keeping you connected and oriented. Premium details like the leather-wrapped shift knob and park brake handle reflect the quality throughout the cabin.  The black 3-piece hard top provides weather protection while maintaining the open-air Gladiator experience you desire. The rear window defroster and sliding window add versatility, while the freedom panel storage bag keeps your gear organized. At 30,200 miles, this Rubicon has been lightly driven and represents excellent value at this stage of its lifecycle.  The Trailer Tow Package equips this truck for serious hauling with its Class IV receiver hitch and trailer hitch zoom capability, supported by the heavy-duty cooling system.
